mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.name: two published identifiers unioned into one primary key by the P-78 StratMap merge
mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.statement: cad_property's 2025 Hays vintage is a UNION of rows keyed on the Hays CAD PropertyID and rows keyed on the TxGIO Prop_ID, which for Hays is a DIFFERENT published identifier for the same parcel. Both id spaces are bare-numeric, so they collide. p78Merge.applyPathAMerge uses coalesce(incoming, existing) with situsAddress, situsCity, situsZip and ownerName in COALESCE_FIELDS, so a colliding StratMap row OVERWRITES a CAD row's address and owner, while assessed_value survives because normalizeStratMapLandUse hardcodes it null. One row then holds CAD account N's money and TxGIO parcel N's address.
mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.priorGrounds: joinNormalize.ts already records that Hays and Williamson do not share a numbering system with their CAD roll, measured by an owner-match gate. Nobody applied that to the CAD-to-CAD join across vintages, and nobody asked whether the merge had copied one side's cells onto the other.

mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.name: renumbering between roll years
mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.statement: Hays CAD renumbered its own accounts between the 2025 and 2026 rolls.

mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.name: genuine parcel resplit
mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.statement: parcels were split or merged, so 2025 and 2026 legitimately describe different things under the same number.

mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.name: coverage-ledger flip lifts the integrity gate
mechanismsEnumeratedBeforeMeasuring.statement: my own hypothesis, added after reading the gate: loadLedgerBlockedFips reads county_facet_coverage WHERE integrity_verdict=block. If the scorer ever ran against a contaminated vintage it would measure high owner agreement and write pass, unblocking the fabricating prop_id join.

instrumentDesign.principle: ENFORCEMENT: a load-bearing claim needs a file-based instrument that has been shown to fail. No shell one-liner produced any number in this close.
instrumentDesign.sqlInstruments: every scan written to a named .sql file under the session scratchpad and run through one runner that SETs default_transaction_read_only and statement_timeout. Each CTE feeding an N-way aggregate is WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED, per CTX-B6's recorded re-inlining lesson.
instrumentDesign.fileInstrument: hays_key_probe.py -- 12 self-test cases run BEFORE any corpus scoring, including two explicit non-vacuity assertions (the stem function must actually strip a prefix; the address normaliser must NOT collapse two different addresses) and three scorer cases proving it reports a miss as a miss, a matched-but-disagreeing row as a disagreement, and an agreeing row as agreement. main() refuses to score a corpus if the self-test fails. A --violate mode inverts every expectation and must exit 1.
instrumentDesign.meaningShapedNotInternalConsistency: the load-bearing test compares two INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED inputs: an identifier published by Hays CAD in its own export file, against an identifier published by TxGIO in a state shapefile. Neither party wrote the other's column. The negative control is Caldwell, whose CAD-to-TxGIO prop_id join is known-good by a third instrument (the owner-match gate) that this lane did not write.
instrumentDesign.whatWouldMakeThisCheckVacuous: if the CAD export and the TxGIO shapefile both derived from one upstream file, agreement between them would prove nothing. They do not: TxGIO's Hays drop is stratmap25-landparcels_48209_hays_202503, a Texas GIO statewide product, and the CAD export is Hays CAD's own Orion output. Named so the reader can check the assumption rather than inherit it.
